==English==
{{phrasebook|en}}
{{was wotd|2016|November|24}}
[[File:Thank You (13824254433).jpg|thumb|A “thank you” sign being held up at a [[conference]] in [[Taiwan]] in 2014]]

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|thanke yow}}; as with {{m|en|thank God}}, {{m|en|praise be to God}}, and {{m|en|praise the Lord}}, it was originally a [[present subjunctive]] form but is usually not parsed that way in current usage. It has also sometimes been parsed as a [[prodrop]] form of ([[present indicative]]) ''I thank you'', a mechanism that may plausibly coexist with the other one (instances being variable).

===Interjection===
{{en-intj}}

# {{non-gloss|An expression of [[gratitude]] or [[politeness]] in response to something done or given.}} {{defdate|from c. 1400}}
#: {{ux|en|“'''Thank you'''!” said the girl after her mom gave her a gift.}}
#: {{ux|en|“And '''thank ''you''''' for being so sweet,” replied her mom.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=attributed to [[w:John Fletcher (playwright)|John Fletcher]]|chapter=[[w:Bonduca|Bonduca, a Tragedy]]|title=The Works of Mr. {{w|Francis Beaumont}}, and Mr. John Fletcher|location=London|publisher=Printed for {{w|Jacob Tonson}}, at Shakespear's Head over-against Catherine-street in the [[w:Strand, London|Strand]]|year=1711|volume=IV|section=act I, scene ii|page=2194|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=3xFEAQAAMAAJ&pg=RA4-PA96|oclc=642500453|passage=''Jun''[''ius''] {{...}} The General has new Wine, new come over. / He muſt have new Acquaintance for it too, / For I will ''none, I '''thank ye'''.'' / ''Pet''[''ilus''] ''None, I '''thank ye'''?'' / A short and touchy answer. ''None, I '''thank ye''''': / Ye do not scorn it, do ye?}}
#* {{RQ:Woolf Mrs Dalloway|passage="But, '''thank you''', Lucy, oh, '''thank you'''," said Mrs. Dalloway, and '''thank you''', '''thank you''', she went on saying (sitting down on the sofa with her dress over her knees, her scissors, her silks), '''thank you''', '''thank you''', she went on saying in gratitude to her servants generally for helping her to be like this, to be what she wanted, gentle, generous-hearted.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|author=w:Benny Andersson; w:Björn Ulvaeus|title=w:Thank You for the Music|album={{w|ABBA: The Album}}|artist=w:ABBA|date=12 December 1977|passage='''Thank you''' for the music, the songs I'm singing / Thanks for all the joy they're bringing / Who can live without it, I ask in all honesty / What would life be? / Without a song or a dance what are we? / So I say '''thank you''' for the music / For giving it to me}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Jerry Goodwin|chapter=Thank You|title=Thank You: One of Seventeen Rules …: Wonderful for Men and Women of All Ages|location=[Philadelphia, Pa.]|publisher=w:Xlibris|year=2007|page=19|isbn=978-1-4257-4126-6|passage=Always say "'''thank you'''." When in doubt, say "'''thank you'''." Say "'''thank you'''" even if you think it is not necessary in the circumstances. Whether the recipient thinks it is or is not, it will be appreciated and remembered. It is impossible to say "'''thank you'''" too often!}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Colin McEvoy; Lynn Olanoff|chapter=13|title=Fatal Jealousy: The True Story of a Doomed Romance, a Singular Obsession, and a Quadruple Murder|series=St. Martin's True Crime Library|location=New York, N.Y.|publisher=[[w:St. Martin's Press|St. Martin's Paperbacks]]|month=February|year=2014|page=136|isbn=978-1-250-00971-5|passage=His return text came about an hour later. "I Love you … For all the right reasons," he wrote. "And I'm glad 2 know u feel the true love u have 4 me again … '''Thank u'''!! You make me feel like i really am superman!!"}}
# {{senseid|en|acceptance of an offer}} {{lb|en|often|with ''[[yes]]''}} {{non-gloss|Used as a polite affirmative to accept an offer.}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|please<id:acceptance of an offer>}}
#: {{ux|en|—May I help you? —Yes, '''thank you'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|—May I help you? —'''Thank you'''.}}
# {{ng|A polite [[dismissal]]; usually used in [[professional]] contexts.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Amy Andrews|title=Limbo|location=Sydney, N.S.W.|publisher=Escape Publishing|year=2015|isbn=978-0-85799-250-5|passage=‘No, come in,’ he said. ‘Martin, right? Have a seat.’ {{...}} ‘'''Thank you''', no, I won’t.’ He moved inside a little more.}}

====Usage notes====
Can also be used in response to an offer not accepted, as if standing for [[no thank you]]. For example, someone offered a bowl full of strawberries after having already eaten a hearty meal might respond with ''I'm full, '''thank you'''.''
